comparison: Both evaluate N160 mutagenesis data (C64, C65, C106-C108). OpenEval finds the data SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers also find it SUPPORTED but note it is 'unsurprising given findings in other Na+/H+ antiporters' and express disappointment that mutagenesis was limited to this residue.

Both address C-terminal tag effects (C118-C122) and cooperativity differences. OpenEval finds the tag explanation SUPPORTED by experimental data. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, noting the attribution of non-cooperativity to His292 absence 'is speculative and could have been tested more thoroughly.'

Both evaluate ion-binding site architecture (C53-C55, C58, C60-C62). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED based on structural homology to PaNhaP. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting 'The protein was crystallized in the presence of sodium, but unfortunately a corresponding density for substrate is not apparent,' indicating lack of direct structural evidence weakens these claims.

Both evaluate functional characterization and kinetics (C8, C9, C66-C70). OpenEval finds data SUPPORTED with reproducible Michaelis-Menten kinetics. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating 'kinetic data...does not seem to be approaching saturation' and 'acridine orange assay...is impossible to quantitatively measure pH change,' questioning the reliability of kinetic parameters and pH profile.

Both address conservation of transport mechanism across antiporters (C91-C93, C96, C100-C101, C113-C115). OpenEval finds structural comparisons SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging useful findings about MjNhaP-PaNhaP similarity but noting broader mechanistic conclusions depend on unconvincing EM structure interpretation.

Both address membrane topology (C28, C29). OpenEval finds topology claims SUPPORTED by GFP/PhoA assays and structural logic. Peer reviewers also find these SUPPORTED as standard experimental approaches, with no concerns raised.

Both evaluate transport rate extrapolation to physiological temperature (C130-C132). OpenEval finds the rate comparison and structural explanation SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly REJECT the temperature extrapolation, stating '500,000 ions per second at 85 degrees...is essentially the turnover rate of an ion channel' and calling it 'misleading speculation' that should be removed.

Both evaluate conformational changes between states (C7, C75-C81). OpenEval finds the 7° tilt and helix movements SUPPORTED by 3D difference maps. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating 'methods used to compare EM map and x-ray model are poorly justified' and noting differences are 'in the direction where the resolution of the EM map is quite limited.'

Both address pH regulation mechanism (C138-C140, C146-C147). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED that Na+ binding, not pH, drives conformational changes. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the MjNhaP-PaNhaP comparison is 'a useful finding' but noting mechanistic conclusions depend on unconvincing EM structure interpretation.

Both evaluate linking structural states to functional conditions (C87-C90) and mechanistic implications (C10-C12, C148-C149). OpenEval finds projection difference maps SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning the conformational change analysis due to limited EM resolution and poorly justified comparison methods.

Both address x-ray structure determination (C3, C4, C30-C33). OpenEval finds crystallization conditions, resolution, and activity data SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers also find structural data SUPPORTED, acknowledging it represents 'inward open' conformation, though they note 'overall significance of the high pH structure alone is not compelling.'

Both evaluate overall architecture (C34-C39). OpenEval finds structural observations SUPPORTED by x-ray structure and valid comparisons to PaNhaP. Peer reviewers also find these SUPPORTED, with no challenges to the structural data itself.

Both evaluate EM structure determination (C5, C6, C72-C74). OpenEval finds crystallization conditions, resolution, and inactivity data SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, expressing 'significant concerns about the EM structure interpretation' and stating results 'are not convincing.'

Both address proposed transport mechanism (C10-C12). OpenEval finds mechanistic conclusions SUPPORTED by structural comparison and conformational changes. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting the rocking bundle mechanism is reasonable but 'underlying structural comparison supporting these mechanistic claims is viewed as unconvincing.'

Both evaluate structural classification of CPA antiporters (C113-C115). OpenEval finds the two-type classification SUPPORTED based on structural comparisons. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, as this classification depends on broader mechanistic conclusions that rely on the questioned EM structure interpretation.

Both address transport mechanism details (C146-C149). OpenEval finds competition for single binding site and rocking bundle mechanism SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging useful findings about pH but noting mechanistic model depends on unconvincing EM structure interpretation.

Both evaluate functional consequences of conformational change (C82-C83, C85-C86). OpenEval finds closure/opening of cytoplasmic/extracellular sides SUPPORTED by structural measurements. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to concerns about EM structure interpretation and limited resolution in the z-direction.

Both address dimer interface architecture, specifically H1 functional importance (C49). OpenEval finds mutational validation SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED with no specific concerns raised about the deletion mutagenesis data.

OpenEval evaluates dimer interface architecture (C44-C47, C49) and finds structural differences from PaNhaP SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers acknowledge overall architecture (including C44) as SUPPORTED but do not specifically comment on dimer interface details.

OpenEval evaluates background claims on sodium/proton antiporters (C1-C2, C13-C20) and finds them SUPPORTED by literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory/background claims.
